alyssa: Heads-up — running into a weird perf regression after the batch-synchronizer change. Long-context runs (8k+ tokens) show periodic latency spikes and memory churn. Initial run: +15% p99 and KV cache growth between merges. Anyone seen similar?
ben: Hmm. Can you paste the profiler output? Is this during merge or split path?
alyssa: Mostly merge. Attaching a short excerpt from the perf sampling (self + kernel):
```
perf: cycles:u  42%   kv_cache::merge_batches
perf: cycles:k  25%   page_fault_handler
flamegraph: kv_slot_reclaim -> pager_lock -> memcpy
softirqs: increased page reclaim events
```
corey: Page fault handler showing up in kernel is a red flag. Could be evictions triggered by batch merge aligning many long contexts and causing KV pages to be scanned. Any evidence of fragment reuse dropping?
lina: I instrumented slot residency counters yesterday — reuse rate drops to ~60% during spikes (normally ~92%). Fragmentation metric (free_slots_per_shard) goes from 120 -> 18.
alyssa: Reproducer (short): run `tools/loadtest --model rwd-open-30b --seq 8k --warm 30s --sustain 120s` with batch-synchronizer enabled. NOTE: disabling synchronizer removes spikes.
ben: Could be HOL (head-of-line) due to the synchronizer grouping requests by latency buckets; long contexts get merged at front and the KV cache reclaimer tries to free space synchronously. That interplay could cause a stall. Do we have logs for KV evict decisions?
alyssa: Yes — here's a relevant snippet from the runtime log around a spike: 
[12:03:21.452] batch-sync: merging 24 reqs (avg len 5600)
[12:03:21.453] kv: need_reclaim: 128MB -> trigger_sync_reclaim
[12:03:21.456] kernel: page_fault: major
[12:03:21.460] batch-executor: waiting on kv_reclaim (12ms)
[12:03:21.480] batch-executor: proceed -> 2ms token generation then next reclaim

corey: That waiting window is your HOL. 12ms stalls in the hot path for the lead batch will serialize subsequent batches, increasing end-to-end p99.
lina: Also saw more small-range memcpy hotspots in flamegraphs when the fragment stitcher runs after reclaim — suggests fragmentation forcing many small copies instead of pointer reuse.
ben: Two possible vectors: (A) synchronizer's merge policy creates large, sudden memory pressure spikes that trigger synchronous reclaim in the critical path; (B) the reclaim path itself is scanning too eagerly and doing full compaction under lock.
alyssa: Agreed. I profiled kv_reclaim: it's taking ~9ms in the fast path but up to 40ms when it does sweep+compact. The compact path grabs the global pager lock.
corey: For short-term mitigation we can: (1) add a micro-delay before merge commit to smooth arrival rates, (2) make reclaim async where possible (background GC with bounded prefetch), or (3) let the synchronizer favor interleaving long contexts instead of forming one big head batch. Which is fastest to test?
ben: (1) is trivial — backpressure buffer for 2-5ms to let KV reclamation happen off the hot path. (2) requires careful correctness work but best long-term. (3) scheduler heuristic change — relatively low-risk.
lina: I can add counters to track when merge_size > threshold && reclaim_mode == sync, so we can detect correlation automatically. Also will add a metric for 'stalled_batch_ms'.
alyssa: I pushed a quick patch that gates merge when avg_seq_len > 4k OR free_slots_per_shard < 32. Deployed to staging. Early results: p99 improved ~6%, total mem growth reduced. But still see occasional spikes.
corey: Nice. Can you also dump per-shard fragmentation histograms during spikes? I suspect a hot shard gets hammered and causes cross-shard steals that are expensive.
alyssa: Will do. Also capturing `kmem: slab_reclaim` traces and `perf record -e page-faults` during repros.
ben: Longer term let's consider: batching heuristics aware of KV state (e.g., `if kv_pressure_high then cap merge_size or prefer splits`), and decouple reclaim to a bounded background worker with soft limits so batch paths only do minimal evict.
lina: Agreed. Will prototype reclaim-asynchronously with a token-based admission (max concurrent reclaim workers = shards/2). If we see no correctness regressions we can flip.
corey: Another observation — kernel OOM killer didn't trigger but swap activity spiked on some nodes -> implies noisy neighbor reclaiming from host. We should also correlate with host-level memory usage and CPU scheduling.
alyssa: Good call. Running cross-node trace now. For immediate next steps: (a) collect shard histograms during a controlled run; (b) run the 2ms merge-delay experiment in prod-sim; (c) instrument sync-reclaim count metrics.
ben: I'll review the reclaim code path and sketch an async design. If we can ensure deterministic slot handoff we can avoid global compaction in hot paths.
nina: oh FYI the infra-bot just reported the staging rollout: `infra-bot: deploy eng-runtime/staging v2026.3.2 -> success`
alyssa: Thanks. Will post findings after next repro. :thumbsup:
